angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 751,356 km at 73.39 pc = 0.14 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.6251 +/- 0.0119 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 73.39 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.08 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 135694 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 751,356 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.02 +/- 0.12 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 135694 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5712 +/- 106 K from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 135694 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 135694 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-135694.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.380, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
